name: Pellene
text: Pellene (; Ancient Greek: Πελλήνη; Doric Greek: Πελλάνα / Πελλίνα) was a city and polis (city-state) of ancient Achaea, the most easterly of the twelve Achaean cities (the Achaean League). Its territory bordered upon that of Sicyon on the east and upon that of Aegeira on the west. Pellene was situated 60 stadia from the sea, upon a strongly fortified hill, the summit of which rose into an inaccessible peak, dividing the city into two parts.

depictions.name: Pellene
depictions.text: Pellene was the easternmost polis of Achaia, a region in Greece. In the 5th century BCE, its outskirts were scavenging grounds for reclaimed lumber, which became a vital part of Achaia's overall ship-building industry based in Patrai. During the Peloponnesian War, Pellene also became the first polis to join Sparta's Peloponnesian League.
